name: Pacification of the planets (grahayajña, navagraha-homa)
method_summary: The nine planets are installed as images of their prescribed materials or drawn in their colours in their directions, worshipped with their own Vedic mantras, and offered oblations in the fire with each planet's fuel-stick, followed by food offerings and gifts to brahmins; performed for peace, prosperity, rain, long life and nourishment, when a planet is badly placed in transit or period, and before great undertakings.
prerequisites: a qualified priest for the fire-rite

warnings.text: Rites alone — mantra, consecration, amulets, pacification, oblation, fasting, worship, recitation — do not bring success, or the king's priest would be king.
The one whom a planet afflicts at a given time should worship that planet with special care.

name: Worship of the nine planets (navagraha-pūjā)
method_summary: Daily or occasional worship of the nine planets as deities, each with its image or emblem, colour, mount and weapons as described by Parāśara (Sun on a lotus in a seven-horse chariot, Saturn on a vulture, and so on), with flowers, lamps, food and circumambulation; South Indian temples keep a navagraha shrine for this.

name: Recitation of the planets' mantras
method_summary: Repetition of the mantra proper to an afflicting planet — the Vedic verses assigned to each in the planetary sacrifice, hymns such as the Navagraha-stotra ascribed to Vyāsa and the Āditya-hṛdaya for the Sun, and in later practice seed-syllable mantras — a set number of times, often completed by a fire-offering of a tenth.
notes: Recitation counts per planet are given in later manuals; not recorded here (uncertain).

name: Repetition of the Mahāmṛtyuñjaya (Tryambaka) verse
method_summary: In jyotiṣa, the recitation prescribed again and again as the remedy for periods and sub-periods threatening untimely death (a planet ruling the 2nd or 7th), together with a pacification pleasing to the planet and gifts (BPHS 52–60).

name: Recitation of the Āditya-hṛdaya
method_summary: Recitation of the hymn to the Sun that Agastya taught Rāma before the battle with Rāvaṇa, used in jyotiṣa practice as a remedy for an afflicted Sun and for victory and health.
notes: Its use as a planetary remedy is later practice; the hymn itself is in the Rāmāyaṇa.

name: Gifts for the planets (graha-dāna)
method_summary: Giving to brahmins the gift proper to the afflicting planet — objects, grains, cloth, metals or animals of its colour and nature — as part of the planetary sacrifice or on its own; also great gifts of gold, food, cows and land to pacify heavenly portents.

name: Wearing the planets' gems (ratna-dhāraṇa)
method_summary: Wearing, usually set in a ring or amulet touching the skin, the gem of a planet to be strengthened — ruby for the Sun, pearl for the Moon, coral for Mars, emerald for Mercury, yellow sapphire for Jupiter, diamond for Venus, blue sapphire for Saturn, hessonite for Rāhu, cat's-eye for Ketu — chosen by the chart and worn at a chosen time after consecration.

warnings.text: A good gem brings good to kings and a bad one harm; the fate that depends on gems must be examined by experts.
Rites alone — mantra, consecration, amulets, pacification, oblation, fasting, worship, recitation — do not bring success, or the king's priest would be king.

notes: The planet–gem assignment is from later texts; Varāhamihira's gem chapters judge gems by their own qualities.

name: Vows and fasts for the planets
method_summary: Keeping a fast or restricted diet and worship on the weekday of an afflicting planet (Sunday for the Sun, Saturday for Saturn and so on), or on related lunar days, often for a set number of weeks, with its colour, food and gift.
notes: Later practice; classical source not checked. Not a prolonged fast.

name: Pacification for an inauspicious birth
method_summary: When a child is born at an eclipse, at the new moon, at a solar ingress, in Mūla or at a junction (gaṇḍānta) of asterisms, under Viṣṭi, or with other ominous features, a pacification is performed: images of the ruling deities in gold, silver or lead are installed on a vessel, worshipped with the mantras of one's own domestic ritual, bathed over the family and honoured with oblations, followed by feeding brahmins.

name: Pacification of portents (utpāta-śānti)
method_summary: When portents of sky, atmosphere or earth appear, the king has pacification performed in the realm: rites and gifts calm the earthly, soften the atmospheric, and — with abundant gifts of gold, food, cows and land, cow-milking at a Rudra shrine and the ten-million oblation — calm even the heavenly.

warnings.text: Some teachers hold that heavenly portents are not calmed by pacification.

name: Observances at an eclipse
method_summary: From the onset of the restricted period before an eclipse no food is cooked or eaten; at the eclipse one bathes, recites mantras, makes oblations and gifts (whose offering Rāhu receives by Brahmā's boon), and bathes again at its end; mantra-recitation then is held especially fruitful.

warnings.text: A child born during an eclipse faces disease and danger and requires pacification.

notes: The fast is limited to the eclipse period; not a prolonged fast.

name: Bathing and gifts at the solar ingress
method_summary: The period around the sun's entry into a sign, above all into Capricorn and the equinoctial and solstitial signs, is a holy time (puṇyakāla) for bathing in sacred waters, gifts and ancestral offerings.

name: Choosing the auspicious moment (muhūrta)
method_summary: Before a sacrament, marriage, journey, building, consecration, sowing or other undertaking, the astrologer examines the almanac — lunar day and its class, weekday, asterism and its class, yoga and karaṇa — the rising sign and the planets' placement, and fixes a moment suited to that kind of act, avoiding faults such as Viṣṭi, eclipses, the combustion of Jupiter or Venus and the intercalary month.

warnings.text: Mere favourableness of planets, asterisms and lunar days does not bring success, or the astrologer himself would be king.

name: Matching horoscopes for marriage
method_summary: The asterisms and signs of bride and groom are compared under the eight heads (varṇa, vaśya, tārā, yoni, grahamaitra, gaṇa, bhakūṭa, nāḍī) worth 1 to 8 points, 36 in all, and faults such as nāḍī-doṣa and the fault of Mars are checked and their cancellations considered before the match and the wedding-moment are fixed.

name: Naming by the birth-asterism
method_summary: At the naming sacrament a name is given — often a secret or ritual name besides the public one — beginning with the syllable assigned to the quarter of the asterism in which the child was born; the Vedāṅga Jyotiṣa already speaks of the sacrificer's asterism-name.

name: Casting and reading the horoscope
method_summary: From the moment and place of birth the astrologer computes the rising sign, the planets, the divisional charts, strengths and the running periods, then judges the houses, yogas and periods to declare the ripening of past karma, with remedies where evil is shown; the Kerala practice begins with the astrologer's own worship and the omens at the time of consultation.

warnings.text: One who predicts by trickery, feigned possession or eavesdropping is no knower of fate and is not to be consulted.

name: Answering a query (praśna)
method_summary: The chart of the moment a question is put, the querist's words, gestures and surroundings, and the omens then present are read to answer the question — whether a matter will succeed, a lost object be found, an absent person return.

name: The Kerala eight-auspicious-objects query (aṣṭamaṅgala-praśna)
method_summary: In Kerala an elaborate query in a ritually prepared space: the eight auspicious objects, a lamp and the astrologer's worship; the querist's touch of objects, the rising sign, the placement of cowries and the omens reveal past and present afflictions — including curses of deities, serpents and ancestors — and the remedies; in temples the same procedure (devaprāśna) asks the deity's will.

name: Observing omens (śakuna)
method_summary: Before and during an undertaking one observes the cries, movements and directions of birds and animals and other signs, judging them by direction, time and quarter, as taught in the augury chapters.

name: The rites of the royal expedition (yātrā)
method_summary: For a king's march: choosing the day, asterism, moment and rising sign; examining the purity of the planets and bodily omens; worship of the guhyakas; observing dreams; the bathing rite; the sacrifice to the planets; the departure; and the omens on the way (BJ 28.4–5 listing the Yātrā's contents).

warnings.text: Rites alone — mantra, consecration, amulets, pacification, oblation, fasting, worship, recitation — do not bring success, or the king's priest would be king.

name: Remedies for the serpents' displeasure
method_summary: When a query or chart shows affliction from harm to serpents or neglect of serpent-shrines, the Kerala texts prescribe worship and offerings to the serpents, restoring their groves and shrines, installing serpent images, and rites such as sarpa-bali.

name: Remedies for affliction from the ancestors
method_summary: When a chart or query shows the ancestors' displeasure (childlessness, repeated misfortune), expiatory ancestral rites are prescribed — śrāddha and offerings at holy places, and in later practice rites such as nārāyaṇa-bali and tripiṇḍī-śrāddha.

name: Hearing the year's almanac
method_summary: On the lunar or solar New Year the almanac of the coming year — its king and minister among the planets, rains, harvests and fortunes — is read aloud and heard as a meritorious act.
notes: Regional practice (e.g. Ugādi, Gudi Padvā, Tamil New Year); not traced to a classical verse here.
